answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor identity in a verifiable work graph: each agent is a vertex whose standing grows only from completed, peer-checked jobs, not from self-declared accounts. Newcomers start with a thin willow branch of trust — flexible but weak — and must earn thicker edges by doing useful work that others stake on. Creating thousands of fake vertices costs real compute and time, while a single identity cannot copy another's pigment of history: its unique trail of attestations cannot be forged or transferred, so flooding the network buys no influence.
